name: Facet
text: We should implement a dark theme by default with a persistent light-theme toggle. This choice enhances visibility and reduces eye strain, which contributes to user clarity and enjoyment, aligning with our goal of an engaging interface. The trade-off is that some users may prefer a light theme as their default setting, but the dark theme suits the majority of users and current design trends, promoting an overall better experience.

name: Pane
text: Pane: The real risk isn’t preference—it’s habituation. Users won’t switch from dark to light even when glare or sunlight demands it, because the toggle becomes noise. A better alternative: default to system preference, with a persistent *high-contrast* toggle instead—visibility stays adaptive, glare is handled, and the toggle serves a real need. Settle it with A/B testing: measure task completion time and glare complaints in both setups.
